question.text: Which of the following is not isostructural with <math><mtext>S</mtext><mtext>i</mtext><mtext>C</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>?</mo></math>

solution.text: In <math><mtext>S</mtext><mtext>i</mtext><mtext>C</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> there is <math><mtext>s</mtext><msup><mrow><mtext>p</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> hybridisation so the structure is tetrahedral. In <math><mtext>S</mtext><msubsup><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mtext>P</mtext><msubsup><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mtext>N</mtext><msubsup><mrow><mtext>H</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> the structure is tetrahedral because in all hybridization is <math><mtext>s</mtext><msup><mrow><mtext>p</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> But in <math><mtext>S</mtext><mtext>C</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mtext>s</mtext><msup><mrow><mtext>p</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>d</mtext></math> hydridisation is present so shape is different which is see saw.
